decisions.reason: The mobile modular waste processing plant concept fits the firm's established recycling-machinery knowledge base and already shows a quantified customer saving, so management would expect to learn further and improve it rather than withdraw it.

A mobile slow-speed shredder is closely related to the firm's core machinery capabilities and its continued standalone presentation in 2024 suggests enough market traction and internal know-how to justify retention.

This modular waste processing concept has the strongest observed validation through a named customer reference and quantified savings, which makes it highly compatible with the firm's absorptive capacity and unlikely to be dropped soon.

The 2024 slow-speed shredders line extends existing shredder know-how, so even with limited public performance evidence the firm would typically keep it to exploit related engineering and market learning.

Mobile spiral shaft screens are still close to the firm's screening and mobile plant competences, but as a newer 2024 launch without visible outcome evidence they carry somewhat higher withdrawal risk than the more validated products.
